summary: Narrow bug fix in @cipherstash/stack's bulk model helpers. Per-field results are keyed by `${modelIndex}-${fieldKey}`; reconstruction previously used `split('-')`, so any field key containing a hyphen was truncated (`some-field` -> `some`) and the encrypted/decrypted value landed under the wrong key while the real field vanished. The change replaces four duplicated blocks (bulkEncryptModels, bulkDecryptModels and both lock-context variants) with one helper that splits at the first hyphen. Because the model index is always a non-negative integer with no hyphen, the first hyphen is always the separator, so the fix is correct for every id the code builds; for hyphen-free keys the output is identical to before. No payload shape, lock-context binding, or operation-result contract changes. A regression test was added for the two non-lock-context paths (not run here; no CI supplied). No material failure scenario introduced by this change was found. Note (pre-existing, not caused by this change): packages/protect/src/ffi/model-helpers.ts still carries the same naive split, and no changeset accompanies the fix.

behaviour_changes.description: Bulk model reconstruction now maps each `${modelIndex}-${fieldKey}` result id back to its full field key by splitting at the first hyphen only. Models whose (possibly nested, dot-joined) field keys contain hyphens now get their encrypted/decrypted values under the correct key instead of a truncated one; models without hyphenated keys are reconstructed exactly as before.
New vitest regression file exercising bulkEncryptModels and bulkDecryptModels with hyphenated column names, against a mocked @cipherstash/protect-ffi.

evidence.claim: fieldsForModelIndex splits each id at the first '-' and keeps the full remainder as the field key.
At base, reconstruction used key.split('-') and took only element [1] as the field key, truncating hyphenated keys (same pattern at 739, 811, 884).
Result ids are built as `${modelIndex}-${fieldKey}` where modelIndex is a numeric array index, so the first hyphen is always the separator.
After extracting per-model fields, keys are split on '.' and written via setNestedValue (unchanged), so nested hyphenated paths are restored correctly.
Regression tests assert hyphenated keys survive bulkEncryptModels and bulkDecryptModels and no truncated keys appear; protect-ffi is mocked; lock-context variants not exercised.
The bulk-encrypt-models operation imports from ../helpers/model-helpers (bulk-decrypt-models.ts:10 likewise).
Backfill calls options.encryptionClient.bulkEncryptModels and uses the returned rows.
The protect package still reconstructs bulk models with key.split('-').
